newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. leads trade mission to Southeast Asia.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. leads trade mission to Southeast Asia.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson announced Thursday that he would lead a trade mission to Southeast Asia in January in hope of opening new markets for exports and increasing foreign investment in the state.
Wilson, a Republican, said he would visit Hong Kong, Taiwan, the Philippines, Indonesia, Thailand, China and Singapore from January 11 through January 31.

Exports to Southeast Asia support more than 250,000 jobs in California, and the growth of exports to this region alone created more than 74,000 new jobs in the state last year, according to the governor's office.
"Now, more than ever, is the time for us to seize the opportunities being presented in Asia to create jobs and strengthen our economy here at home," Wilson said.

International trade is becoming an increasingly important part of the state's economy, with 25 percent of the state's $904 billion gross state product supported by exports and foreign investment, Wilson's office said.
Exports alone are valued at $96 billion annually, with many Asian countries dominating the list of California's top export markets.
Although Japan and Korea are two of the state's top trading partners, Wilson said the trade mission would focus primarily on markets that offer growth opportunities.

Wilson said he would be joined in Asia by members of his cabinet, including the secretary of the state trade and commerce agency, and business leaders interested in expanding their operations in Southeast Asia.
In 1993, Wilson visited Asia, including Japan and Korea, and secured more than $200 million in foreign investment for the state.
